places.name: Yên Quang Các
places.size: The old founding seat of a minor alchemists-and-pickers sect (moved in 1187 to Dã Tang Lâm), now called the Dusk Field: about 20 buildings in a small walled yard about 150 m across, the outer gate, the founder's grave and a pickers' sunset field of open hillside.
places.where: Region 13 (Ngư Ca Xuyên), steppe at 0.2 km. On the map, gold-and-green rolling steppe hills with a winding river at the right edge and a streak of rust-orange ground at the lower left; no sea. Vassal of Lạc Hà Tông, righteous. The sect moved away in 1187 and this is the Dusk Field. Nearest: hot spring Hà Quang Tuyền (146 km), spirit vein Khoáng Dã Mạch (224 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Sunset: pickers walk the golden hillside in a slow line with baskets, a haze of pale light lies on the grass, and an old woman sweeps the founder's grave.
places.subject: The place: Yên Quang Các, the Pavilion of the Hazy Light, the old seat of a small alchemists' sect, now the Dusk Field. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at sunset; rolling steppe hills of tawny gold and green grass fill the frame, combed by the wind, with a single blue river winding down from the top right in tight bends and a faint trail looping across the slopes; a rust-orange patch of ground shows at the lower left, and the whole slope is lit with a soft hazy glow that gives the place its name. The yard: about twenty small buildings of grey stone and grey tile in a low walled enclosure, now quiet: a gate-house with a double roof facing the road, a plain hall with a lantern hung before it, a long drying shed where bundles of herbs and bark hang in rows, a small furnace house, a well, and a handful of keepers' houses with thin smoke. Signature element: on the open hillside behind the wall, the founder's grave, a mound of earth with a single upright stone and a ring of white pebbles, and below it the Dusk Field itself, a broad gentle slope where about thirty tiny pickers in straw hats walk in a slow line at sunset through the long grass, bending to gather evening herbs, each trailing a long soft shadow. A few young cypresses mark the path to the gate. Life at scale: a hushed, small, gold-lit place that is half pasture and half remembering. Light: low hazy gold sunset light from the upper left, long shadows, a warm mist glowing in the hollows.

places.name: Vân Kiều Trấn
places.size: A great sect's present seat since 1185, built over and around the ruins of an older mountain bridge-town: a domain about 4 km across on a high mountain, about 300 halls, bridges and terraces, with about 3,000 residents (disciples, servants, artisans, caravan families). Rebuilt grandly on old stones.
places.where: Region 13 (Ngư Ca Xuyên), high mountain at 0.6 km. On the map a rugged range of pale grey rock ridges and dark conifer forest with green meadow pockets and rust-orange slopes, a thin stream threading the valley; no sea. Lạc Hà Tông, one of the seven great sects, moved its seat here from the steppe in 1185. Nearest: peak Đoạn Liên Phong (135 km), spirit vein Cổ Bách Mạch (152 km), mine Kim Sa Khoáng (168 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: Evening on the great stone bridges: the sect's lanterns glow rose across a chasm, and old black arches of the former town show through the new pale terraces.
places.subject: The place: Vân Kiều Trấn, the Cloud Bridge Town, now the seat of the Sect of the Drifting Sunset Clouds, built into a high rugged mountain valley. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at evening; a range of pale grey ridges and serrated crags runs across the frame, dark conifer forest filling the folds, green meadow pockets and rust-orange slopes among the rock, a thin stream winding through the valley floor and low cloud pooled in the gullies. The sect: a domain about four kilometres across spread over three ridges and the valley between them, some three hundred buildings in rose-tiled halls of pale stone with ochre terrace walls, stepping up the slopes in broad terraces and clinging to ledges; the old bridge-town lies beneath and among them: dozens of ancient dark stone arches and half-rebuilt spans, black with age, crossing gorges between the ridges, some carrying roads and some now carrying halls; a great new pale stone bridge, three hundred paces long, joins the two main ridges at the height of the roofs, with covered pavilions at its piers. Signature element: the bridges, forty of them in all, dark old and pale new in a lattice across the gorges, with tiny lantern-bearers on them, and the sect's halls turned toward the west where a gap in the range shows the red sky; mist rises under the arches. Life at scale: thousands of tiny residents on stairs, bridges and terraces, caravans on the valley road. Light: red-gold evening light from the upper left on the rose roofs, deep blue shadows in the gorges, lanterns beginning to glow.

places.name: Thiên Xu Tông
places.size: The oldest great sect's seat: a domain about 6 km long down a curving mountain ridge, seven terraced halls in the line of the Northern Dipper plus about 500 other buildings (barracks, array halls, scripture halls, workshops), with about 4,000 residents (disciples, servants, artisans, mortal families). The strongest sect of the continent.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên, the heart of the continent), high mountain at 2.07 km. On the map a spine of bare grey-white crags with a rust-red upper shoulder running north-south, bounded by brown-green highland slopes with a small round lake at the left edge; no sea. Earth 33 %, metal 29 %. Held by Thiên Xu Tông, enforcer of the North Star Compact. Nearest: mine Trận Thạch Khoáng (79 km), peak Xu Trụ Phong (103 km), Hoa Cái Đường (127 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: The last light of the day: the black-iron spire of the Pivot Hall catches the sun long after the valleys are dark, and below it the seven halls step down the ridge like a great bent dipper of gold lamps.
places.subject: The place: Thiên Xu Tông, the Sect of the Heavenly Pivot, on a bare high mountain above the heart of the continent. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at the end of the day; a long spine of grey-white serrated crags curves across the frame, with a shoulder of rust-red rock on its upper east flank and thin green and tawny highland slopes on both sides, a round blue lake in the brown plateau at the far left, and valleys already in blue shadow. The sect: seven great terraced halls step down the curving ridge in the exact bent line of the Northern Dipper, each a little lower than the last, each as large as a palace, with broad stone terraces, double and triple roofs of dark grey tile, long covered stairs, and pale granite walls built straight into the cliffs; the first and highest, the Pivot Hall, carries a slender black-iron spire, about a hundred paces tall, that catches the last light; the seventh stands at the ridge's tail. Between the halls and on both flanks stretch about five hundred lesser buildings: array halls with great carved floors, scripture libraries, long barracks of the sect's strictest discipline, forges, a harbour of pilgrims' hostels, kitchens and gardens held on terraces; a processional road of grey stone runs down the length of the ridge. Signature element: the seven halls in Dipper formation with their lights coming on, and a faint pale line of array glow tracing between them across the ridge. Life at scale: four thousand tiny figures on terraces and stairs, long caravan trains at the foot. Light: low gold-red evening light from the upper left on the iron spire and the gilt eaves, long blue shadows filling the valleys.

places.name: Củng Tinh Quán
places.size: A minor sect of formation masters and star-diviners, about 50 Daoists and lay servants: a quiet walled abbey of about 30 low dark-tiled buildings about 150 m across beside a round mountain lake, with an open platform bearing a great bronze armillary.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), highland at 1.36 km. On the map a brown-green high plateau of rolling folds with a round blue lake and a thin river leaving it to the south, grey crags along the left and upper right edges; no sea. Vassal of Thiên Xu Tông, neutral. Nearest: lake Phong Văn Hồ (90 km), lake Tinh Lạc Hồ (177 km), mine Vẫn Tinh Khoáng (195 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Night: the bronze armillary turns against a field of stars while the abbey's lamps are all dimmed, and a single reader notes the angle of a ring.
places.subject: The place: Củng Tinh Quán, the Abbey of the Bowing Stars, a quiet abbey beside a round mountain lake. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk; a high open plateau of brown and green folded highland rolls across the frame, wind-cropped and treeless, with a round dark-blue lake, about two kilometres across, lying in a hollow to the right and a thin river leaving it to the south; bare grey crags stand along the left and upper edges, and the first stars show in a violet sky. The abbey: about thirty low buildings of dark grey tile and plain pale stone inside a low wall, arranged in a precise square around a main court: a meditation hall, a library of star-tables, two dormitories, a kitchen, a drying yard, an observatory shed with a sliding roof, a small shrine, and a few lay servants' houses; the roofs are low so as not to block the sky. Signature element: in the middle of the main court, on a raised stone platform open to the sky, turns a great bronze armillary of nested rings, about ten paces across, green with age, its pointer fixed on the pole star, with long thin shadows of the rings across the court; about a dozen tiny Daoists in dark robes stand around it with tablets, and a few more on the lake's shore watching the water, where the first stars already lie. Life at scale: a hushed, ascetic place of watching. Light: deep blue-violet dusk with a last warm gold on the western crags from the upper left, the lake dark as glass, one lantern burning.

places.name: Thiên Quyền Thị
places.size: A great square market at the foot of the Pivot's mountain: about 200 grey stone halls and about 1,500 stalls around a square about 250 m across, with several thousand traders and pilgrims on a market day; a locked hall of standard weights.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), grassland at 0.44 km. On the map, the foot of a bare grey spine of crags with a rust-red shoulder, broken brown-green highland to the left and tawny-green slopes to the right, a thin stream at the lower left; no sea. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; opened in 200. Nearest: peak Thạch Quyền Phong (90 km), mine Hoàng Đồng Khoáng (100 km), mine Trận Thạch Khoáng (141 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Spring test day: a ceremonial line of officials brings the standard weights out of the locked hall, and the traders wait nervously beside their scales.
places.subject: The place: Thiên Quyền Thị, the Market of the Heavenly Balance, a great square market below the Pivot's mountain. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright cold spring morning; at the upper left a bare grey serrated spine of crags with a rust-red shoulder rises above the market, brown-green highland folds roll away to the left and tawny-green slopes to the right, and a thin stream passes at the lower left. The market: a perfectly square layout of about two hundred grey stone halls and about fifteen hundred stalls in neat rows around a square about two hundred and fifty paces across, with four broad avenues entering at the middle of the sides, caravans' yards with ox wagons at each gate, assayers' offices, a measurers' hall with a locked weights vault of thick stone, and clean grey arcades; the hall's roofs are dark and low. Signature element: in the middle of the square stands a tall timber gantry, about thirty paces high, from which hangs a giant bronze steelyard whose beam is as long as a boat, green-bronze with huge pans of dark metal; a crowd of about eight hundred tiny figures surrounds it in a ring; before the vault door a short ceremonial procession carries a small chest of standard weights toward the square. Life at scale: thousands of traders in orderly lines, carts of ore and cloth, a hum of fairness. Light: crisp, cold, clear light from the upper left, sharp shadows of the arcades and gantry, the grey crags glowing behind.

places.name: Thạch Kiều Thành
places.size: The first city of the heart, a walled river city of about 50,000 people: walls about 2.5 km on a side, some 11,000 grey roofs in a grid, crossing the river on one great stone bridge about 400 m long with two bell towers.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), steppe at 0.87 km on a river. On the map, rolling golden-green steppe hills with a winding blue river running from left to right and rust-brown pockets in the upper left; grey rock at the lower edge; no sea. Held by Thiên Xu Tông. The North Star Compact was set here in 510. Nearest: spirit vein Kiều Cơ Mạch (75 km), ruin Minh Sa Các (79 km), mine Ngân Sa Khoáng (212 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Compact day: every bell in the city is left silent and yet hums in the wind, and the long bridge's dark old arches stand against its pale new deck.
places.subject: The place: Thạch Kiều Thành, the Stone Bridge City, the first city of the heart. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear afternoon; rolling steppe of golden-green hills with scattered dark clumps, a winding blue river running across the frame from left to right in loose bends, and bare grey rock peeping at the lower edge. The city: a walled grid of about eleven thousand grey-tile roofs inside grey stone walls about two and a half kilometres on a side with towers, laid out in tight blocks on both banks, with a vast central market square, guild halls of the four coasts, caravanserais with large yards, warehouses on the banks, a hall of the ruling sect with a broad court, and a quarter of tall narrow houses. Signature element: one great stone bridge, about four hundred paces long and twenty wide, carries the main road across the river between the two halves of the city; its old central arches are dark, almost black, with age, while the wide new deck and outer arches added in 1050 are pale grey, so the bridge is two-toned like a banded snake; a stone bell tower stands at each end, tall and slender, with bronze bells silent in the open belfries; the bridge deck is thick with tiny carts and walkers. Life at scale: tens of thousands of tiny residents, caravans, barges under the arches. Light: warm gold afternoon light from the upper left, the river sparkling, soft long shadows of the towers.

places.name: Mộc Hương Thôn
places.size: A woodcutters' village of about 150 people: about 35 steep grey-roofed houses on a river bank under incense-tree groves, with a row of about 10 low clay curing kilns along the water.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), temperate forest at 0.11 km on a river. On the map: dark conifer forest and golden-green meadow hills, a blue river winding through with a side-stream, grey rock at the lower-left corner; no sea. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; scented wood goes to the Pivot Hall since 600. Nearest: beast lair Thiết Đề Nguyên (75 km), town Bích Khê Trấn (168 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: Morning: the thin blue smoke of the curing kilns hangs over the river and smells sweet a long way downstream, and a log wrapped in yellow cloth is carried to a cart.
places.subject: The place: Mộc Hương Thôn, the Wood Scent Village, a woodcutters' village under incense-tree groves. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a still morning; dark conifer forest and gold-green meadow hills fill the frame, a blue river winding through them with a small side-stream joining in a loop at the top, a pale grey outcrop at the lower-left corner and a little round pond. The village: about thirty-five houses with steep grey-tile roofs on the river bank and a gentle slope, each in a small yard with stacked fuel and a drying rack, narrow lanes, a plain hall, a sawmill with a small wheel on the side-stream; around the village stand groves of tall incense trees, tall and slim, with pale bark and dark crowns, with young saplings planted in tidy rows beside each stump, a sapling for every log. Signature element: along the water in a row stand ten low clay curing kilns, beehive-shaped and cream-grey, each with a thin plume of blue smoke that merges into one blue haze lying over the river and drifting downstream; stacked logs in curing yards beside them; at the kilns' end a single log wrapped in yellow cloth lies on a cart ready to leave for the Pivot. Tiny woodcutters with long saws and a few oxen in the grove. Life at scale: small, quiet, fragrant, hard-working. Light: soft pale gold morning light from the upper left through the smoke haze, soft shadows of the incense trees.

places.name: Thụ Âm Thôn
places.size: A village of about 200 people under the canopy of one vast old tree about 120 m across: about 45 grey-roofed houses in cool dappled shade, goats tethered to the tree's roots.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), temperate forest at 0.23 km on a river. On the map: gold-green meadows with dark conifer, a river running down the middle, a large round patch of rust-red broken ground at the right and grey crags at the lower left; no sea. Held by Thiên Xu Tông, near the poisoned plain left by the battle of Chiết Kích Nguyên. Nearest: spirit vein Bàn Căn Mạch (75 km), city Thanh Bách Thành (158 km), ruin Khô Tỉnh Trấn (190 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: A clear day: from the far edge of the shade a villager looks out over the gold plain, where a grey haze lies low in the distance.
places.subject: The place: Thụ Âm Thôn, the Tree Shade Village, sheltering whole under one vast old tree. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear day; gold-green meadow hills with dark conifer groves, a river winding down the middle of the frame, a great round patch of rust-red broken ground to the right and bare grey crags at the lower left, and at the top, far off on the plain, a thin grey haze of miasma lying low. The village: one tree of enormous size at the centre, its single crown about a hundred and twenty paces across, a dense dark-green dome, and beneath it, glimpsed only through gaps in the leaves, about forty-five grey-tile roofs dappled with light and shade, with narrow cool lanes between them, a well at the trunk's foot, a small shrine in the roots, and long goat-pens; the crown's edge casts a huge round shadow on the grass, with the village's field plots and small vegetable gardens laid out around the shadow's rim. Signature element: the tree itself, never pruned, with a fallen branch burned on a stone pyre beside it, and about thirty goats tethered at the roots, each by a short rope, tiny pale dots; from the far edge of the shade a tiny child looks toward the grey haze, a mother's hand on his shoulder. Life at scale: a small cool community in a shadow the size of a hill. Light: strong gold clear light from the upper left, the shadow of the tree long and dark across the meadow, the haze pale at the horizon.

places.name: Thần Sa Khoáng
places.size: A cinnabar mine: a hillside cut into about 20 stepped terraces of vermilion spoil, each with a shallow washing pool, about 25 sheds and a low furnace house for about 200 miners; the works about 600 m across.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), badlands at 0.54 km. On the map: tawny-green hills and ridges stained rust-red and orange with cinnabar, a patch of pale grey crags at the right and a little tarn among them, a thin stream at the left; no sea. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; cinnabar found in 300, the alchemists' first stone. Nearest: mine Hồng Câu Khoáng (103 km), spring Đan Nhũ Thang (106 km), peak Hồng Nha Phong (125 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: Midday: every washing pool on the terraces runs a different red, and the miners kneel at a stone trough rinsing their hands before eating.
places.subject: The place: Thần Sa Khoáng, the Cinnabar Mine, in red badlands. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at midday; hills of tawny grass and rust-red and orange rock, tinted with cinnabar dust, fill the frame, with a few pale grey crags and a small blue tarn at the right and a thin stream winding down the left side. The mine: one hillside is cut into about twenty broad stepped terraces of bright vermilion spoil, each a shelf about fifty paces wide and the colour of fresh blood, with a shallow stone-lined washing pool on every step in which the cinnabar is rinsed, the pools in shades from orange to deep crimson, linked by narrow spillways; at the hill's foot a low stone furnace house squats under a wide chimney, with a thread of pale smoke, an ore yard with sacks, a settling tank, a tool shed and two rows of miners' huts; carts on a rutted red track. Signature element: the staircase of red terraces and pools, the brightest colour on the whole hill, with its reflection of the sky; a stone trough at the foot where about thirty tiny miners in cloth masks rinse their hands in a line before eating; red dust on their clothes and on the nearest roofs. Life at scale: about two hundred tiny workers climbing and carrying, small against the hill. Light: bright midday sun from the upper left, hot saturated colours, short sharp shadows, a faint red haze over the works.

places.name: Lưu Hoàng Khoáng
places.size: A sulphur mine: a floor of yellow crust pans about 2 km across with steaming fissures, about 15 low stone scraping-sheds and a gong; no permanent housing, workers in shifts of about 100.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), badlands at 0.37 km. On the map: a jagged mass of pale grey rock ridges at the left, a swathe of rust-red ridge in the middle, tawny-green hills at the right, a tarn at the upper left and a thin stream at the right; no sea. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; mined since 420 for fire powders. Nearest: spirit vein Địa Hỏa Mạch (103 km), mine Trận Thạch Khoáng (212 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: A hot shift change: the gong sounds as the fissures breathe harder, and a line of masked workers hurries off the yellow crust.
places.subject: The place: Lưu Hoàng Khoáng, the Sulphur Mine, a yellow crust floor in grey badlands. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at midday; a jagged range of pale grey rock ridges rises at the left, a swathe of rust-red ridges lies across the middle and tawny-green hills at the right, with a small blue tarn high on the left and a thin stream winding at the far right. The mine: in a basin among the ridges spreads a grey badland floor on which flat pans of yellow sulphur crust spread like pale lemon sheets, each a hundred paces across, ringed with stained bands of white, rust and orange as if painted by rings, and broken by steaming fissures from which white vapour drifts in thin curtains; about fifteen low stone sheds with flat roofs stand on the pan edges where the crust is scraped and bagged into hide sacks, with a wide gong frame at the largest shed, and a rough ox-track leading out. Signature element: the ground stained in concentric rings of yellow, white and rust around each fissure, and a line of about forty tiny workers in cloth masks scraping crust in the nearest pan, while others carry sacks on poles, a thin pale vapour all around them. The air looks hazy and heavy; no tree stands within the basin. Life at scale: a harsh, temporary, dangerous place worked in shifts. Light: hard bright midday sun from the upper left, the yellow crust glaring, a pale smell-haze softening the ridges.

places.name: Vẫn Tinh Khoáng
places.size: A star-iron mine: a shallow round crater about 400 m across on a high plateau, a timber headframe and winch over the deepest shaft, about 10 sheds and about 120 miners; stone cairns on the rim.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), highland at 1.42 km. On the map: brown-green high plateau folds with a round blue lake at the right and a thin river from it, grey crags along the left; no sea. Held by Củng Tinh Quán; star iron has been dug here since 160. Nearest: village Tầm Dược Thôn (190 km), Củng Tinh Quán (195 km), lake Phong Văn Hồ (206 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: A clear cold night: the abbey's star-readers lie along the crater rim sighting stars, the headframe black against the Dipper.
places.subject: The place: Vẫn Tinh Khoáng, the Fallen Star Mine, a crater mine on a high plateau. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk; a high open plateau of brown and green wind-cropped folds, treeless, with a round blue lake at the right and a thin river leaving it to the south, bare grey crags along the left edge and deep violet sky above. The mine: a shallow round crater, about four hundred paces across, lined with dark, rust-streaked rock the colour of old iron, its rim a low ring of broken stone; at the crater's centre the deepest shaft opens under a timber headframe, about twenty paces tall, with a winch house and an iron bucket on a chain; around the shaft, tiers of spoil in rust and black, a narrow track spiralling down the crater wall, ore carts, a smelting shed with a dull red glow and a thin plume, about ten sheds, and long rows of stacked star-iron ingots under a canvas; miners' huts of stone and turf on the plain beyond. Signature element: small stone cairns spaced round the crater rim like a ring of marker teeth, about forty of them, and tiny figures in dark robes, the abbey's star-readers, standing at some of them with sighting rods aimed at the first stars. Life at scale: about a hundred and twenty tiny miners, the crater large as a lake bed. Light: deep dusk blue with a last copper-gold glow on the rim from the upper left, the shaft a black circle, forge glow warm in the dimness.

places.name: Tinh Lạc Hồ
places.size: A natural site: a dark, perfectly round lake about 2 km across, rimmed by a single ring of pale stones, on a high plateau; no buildings, at most a herders' tent and a keeper's hut far on the rim.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), lake at 1.18 km. On the map: a round blue lake in a brown-green folded high plateau with a thin river leaving it to the south, grey crags at the right edge; no sea. Beside Củng Tinh Quán; no sect holds it. Nearest: lake Bán Nguyệt Hồ (75 km), lake Phong Văn Hồ (90 km), village Thanh Khoa Thôn (141 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: A windless night: the whole Northern Dipper lies in the black water star for star, and at the rim a herder whispers a wish.
places.subject: The place: Tinh Lạc Hồ, the Lake Where the Stars Fall, a high round lake that holds the sky. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at deep dusk, the last hour before full night; a high bare plateau of brown and green wind-cropped folds, treeless, with a few grey crags at the right edge, and a thin stream leaving the lake's southern end. The lake: a dark, perfectly round sheet of water about two kilometres across, so still that it reads as black glass; around its whole shore runs a single ring of pale stones, laid by hand, each the size of a loaf, in an unbroken circle; on the water, with stars just beginning to come out in a violet sky, the Northern Dipper and the nearest stars appear reflected exactly, seven points of silver, star for star, so clear that the lake looks like a window to a second sky. Signature element: the reflection and the ring of pale stones; no boat, no ripple, no fisherman; on the rim at the south side a single small herders' tent with a thin thread of smoke and a lone figure at the water's edge, kneeling, whispering, with a flock of a hundred sheep, tiny pale dots, on the slope; on the far north rim a small stone keeper's hut with a lantern, where the abbey's star-readers come. Life at scale: stillness itself, the scale of a lake and the sky. Light: deep violet dusk, a last faint gold on the plateau from the upper left, a few early stars, silver reflections.

places.name: Thương Ưng Đài
places.size: A natural site: a high flat-topped stone table about 1.2 km across and 150 m tall, ringed on its cliff rim with about 300 stick nests of grey hawks; at most a hunters' camp of two tents far below.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), highland at 1.71 km. On the map: tawny and green highland ridges with rust-red pockets, dark conifer groves at the lower left, pale grey crags along the left and bottom, a thin stream and small ponds at the top; no sea. No sect holds it; the hunting ground of the grey hawks near Chiết Kích Nguyên. Nearest: mine Tập Trận Khoáng (90 km), spring Hoàng Yên Tuyền (152 km), mine Thanh Kim Khoáng (158 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Midday: hundreds of grey hawks wheel above the table in a slow spinning ring, and a young climber crouches at the rim reaching for a chick.
places.subject: The place: Thương Ưng Đài, the Grey Hawk Terrace, a stone table on the high plateau. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at midday; a high plateau of tawny and green ridges with rust-red pockets and a few dark conifer groves fills the frame, with pale grey crags along its left and bottom edges and a thin stream winding past little ponds at the top. The terrace: a high flat-topped stone table about twelve hundred paces across and as tall as a great tower, with sheer pale cliffs on every side, rising from the plateau like a stage; its top is scoured to bare grey rock by the wind, without a blade of grass; round the whole cliff rim, about three hundred great stick nests of grey hawks sit in rows on every ledge and crack, each nest as wide as a cart, grey and brown with white droppings streaking the stone below. Signature element: the hawks, about two hundred grey birds circling above the table in a slow spiral, casting small shadows across the top, with more perched on the rim; at one corner of the rim a tiny climber on a rope, reaching toward a nest; far below on the plain a hunters' camp of two small tents with a thread of smoke and a cluster of tiny figures looking up. Life at scale: the table is enormous and the birds like flakes of ash. Light: bright clear midday light from the upper left, hard shadows of the cliffs on the plateau, the wind visibly combing the grass.

places.name: Thạch Quyền Phong
places.size: A natural site: a mountain mass about 15 km across with a spine of pale grey crags and a long dark conifer band, crowned by one great weight-shaped peak; at most a small cairn shrine and a path.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), high mountain at 1.24 km. On the map: a round turquoise lake at the left edge, a green-gold plain with a stream, a long band of dark conifers climbing a ridge beside a spine of pale grey crags, rust-orange hills and green meadows on the right; no sea. No sect holds it. The depth pages: the Pivot's Stone Weight Peak. Nearest: market Thiên Quyền Thị (90 km), mine Hoàng Đồng Khoáng (90 km), mine Tinh Kính Khoáng (106 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Morning: the peak, shaped like a heavy standard weight, stands over a band of dark conifers, and a single pilgrim stands at its foot.
places.subject: The place: Thạch Quyền Phong, the Stone Weight Peak, a great mountain shaped like a standard weight. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear morning; a green-gold plain with a winding stream lies at the left, a round turquoise lake at the far left edge, and a long band of dark conifer forest climbs a ridge toward a spine of pale grey crags; to the right rust-orange hills and green meadows stretch away. The peak: a huge mountain mass about fifteen kilometres across, its summit a single squat, broad-shouldered block of pale grey rock with steep sides and a flat top like a great weight-stone or a drum, the largest peak in the frame, ringed by lesser crags like sentinels; snow lies in the cracks and gullies; shelves of scree slope down on every side to the conifer band, which narrows to a dark ribbon; the east side is rust-orange. Signature element: the peak's form, a block of stone as plain and heavy as the weights kept in the market below, casting a long clean shadow across the plain to the lower right; a narrow foot-path winds up from the lake to a tiny cairn shrine of stacked grey stones at its foot, and a single pilgrim in grey stands beside it. No halls, no roofline. Life at scale: an enormous heavy silence. Light: clear gold morning light from the upper left on the grey crags, long cool shadows over the plain, the lake glinting.

places.name: Hoa Cái Đường
places.size: A minor sect of about 60 refiners, washers and sellers: a walled forest-slope settlement of about 45 buildings about 250 m across, with a ring of canopy furnaces, five tiles (about 125 km) below the Pivot's seat.
places.where: Region 14 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên), temperate forest at 1.73 km on a slope. On the map: a long band of dark conifers on a ridge beside a pale grey crag spine, a turquoise lake at the left with a stream running out, golden-green meadow, rust-orange hills at the upper right; no sea. Vassal of Thiên Xu Tông, righteous. Nearest: ruin Tây Quan Bảo (79 km), mine Tinh Kính Khoáng (90 km), peak Thạch Quyền Phong (125 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: A cold night: the canopy furnaces glow under tall star-shaped bronze lids and the refiners' breath hangs in the air between the pines.
places.subject: The place: Hoa Cái Đường, the Hall of the Canopy Star, a forest-slope sect of refiners. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk; a long band of dark conifer forest climbs a steep ridge, a spine of pale grey crags rising beside it, a round turquoise lake with a stream at the left and green-gold meadow around it, and rust-orange hills at the upper right. The sect: about forty-five buildings of grey stone and dark tile on a forest slope inside a stout wall of piled stone, in four tiers cut into the hillside among the pines: a main hall with a double roof, a library and an oath hall, long refiners' sheds, washing yards where ore is rinsed by a leat of stream water, a seller's court with stalls, apprentices' houses and a few households. Signature element: a ring of about nine canopy furnaces, each a squat round furnace housed under a tall bronze star-shaped lid like a great umbrella, set around the central court, glowing orange at their edges and breathing thin smoke through slots in the canopies, the lids shining like a constellation of gilt discs from above; around them stacked charcoal, slag piles and bundles of ore. About thirty tiny refiners in leather aprons and washers at the leat. Life at scale: a small, orderly, fire-lit settlement in the pines. Light: deep blue dusk with the last gold on the crags from the upper left, the furnaces' orange glow warm against the dark forest.

places.name: Thối Tinh Môn
places.size: A minor sect of weapon forgers, about 60 smiths, miners and apprentices: a settlement of about 45 soot-dark stone halls climbing a steep mountain flank about 300 m long, beside a cascade of about 20 stone quenching troughs.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 0.88 km. On the map: a huge mass of bare grey and white serrated ridges with a stream cutting through and a snow-white crest, a few small tarns, rust-orange pockets at the right; no sea. Vassal of Thiên Xu Tông, neutral. Nearest: ruin Lang Yên Bảo (90 km), peak Thiết Châm Phong (150 km), mine Mã Não Quật (168 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: A blade is plunged and a column of white steam bursts from the third trough; the whole slope seems to smoke, and smiths in black aprons lean on their tongs.
places.subject: The place: Thối Tinh Môn, the Gate of the Quenched Stars, a forging sect on a steep mountain flank. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at mid-afternoon; a great mass of bare grey and white serrated ridges crowds the frame, snow along its crests, a few small blue tarns in the hollows, with a stream cutting down the flank and rust-orange scree pockets at the right. The sect: about forty-five buildings of soot-dark stone with black-tile roofs climbing the slope in five tiers, stepped into the rock, around a main forge hall, a hall of oaths, smiths' dwellings, ingot stores of star iron, a small weapon-testing yard with racks of straw targets, miners' barracks and a few shared kitchens; one small forge hall at the side stands swept and cold with its door shut, never used again. Signature element: down the middle of the slope runs a long cascade of about twenty stone quenching troughs, each spilling into the next, fed by a stream led off the mountain, and white steam bursts from each trough whenever a blade is plunged, so that columns of steam rise at several places along the stair, drifting up the slope; the whole mountainside seems to smoke. About thirty tiny smiths and apprentices in black leather aprons carry glowing blades on tongs between the troughs. Life at scale: a loud, hot, soot-blackened little town among cold white rock. Light: bright cold afternoon light from the upper left on the snow crests, long blue shadows in the gullies, the steam gleaming white and the forge-glow red.

places.name: Phất Y Cốc
places.size: A minor sword sect of about 120 swords, most out on hire at any time: a modest settlement of about 40 plain timber halls behind a tall stone gate with a blank name board, about 250 m across in a high valley.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), grassland valley at 1.02 km. On the map: tawny-green high valley slopes at the left, a river winding down the middle with small tarns, grey serrated peaks and snow-streaked crags on the right; no sea. Vassal of Thiên Xu Tông, righteous. Nearest: gorge Vạn Trùng Hạp (103 km), mine Lệ Thạch Khoáng (125 km), mine Lam Lục Khoáng (200 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: Dawn: a swordsman passes out under the blank board without a word, brushes his sleeve and walks down the valley road alone.
places.subject: The place: Phất Y Cốc, the Valley of the Brushed Sleeve, a sword sect in a high green valley. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dawn; a high valley of tawny-green grass slopes runs down the left of the frame, a clear river winding down its middle past a few small blue tarns, and grey serrated peaks with snow in their cracks ring the right side. The sect: about forty plain timber halls with dark grey-tile roofs and no ornament at all, set around a bare central court of pale gravel and behind a tall stone gate; the gate is wide and high, with a long wooden name board over it left deliberately blank, a pale empty rectangle; inside, a long hall, two dormitories, a mess hall, a forge for the sect's own blades, a drill yard with plain wooden rails, a stable for the hiring horses, a few huts for visiting patrons who come to hire swords. Signature element: the blank board over the gate, and a trail of lone swordsmen passing out and in beneath it in ones and twos without a word: about ten tiny figures in plain grey, spaced well apart on the road, each with a single sword, one pausing to brush a sleeve; no names carved on anything, no banners, no trophies. Life at scale: sparse, plain, silent; fewer people at home than the halls could hold. Light: pale clear dawn light from the upper left on the snow peaks, soft shadows, mist on the river, the road silver.

places.name: Tinh Hán Thành
places.size: The great inland-sea port of Thiên Xu: a walled city of about 45,000 people, walls about 2.4 km on a side, about 10,000 grey roofs in a grid, behind a curving breakwater of sea-serpent bones about 1.5 km long; a harbour with about 100 vessels.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), steppe at sea level on a river mouth, coast and port on the inland sea. On the map: green-and-gold hills with a thin river running to the shore of a big deep-blue sea at the right, grey crags at the bottom and top right. Founded by Thiên Xu Tông in 260 on the reef left by a sea-serpent a nameless swordsman killed in 15. Nearest: spirit vein Triều Tịch Mạch (90 km), village Thủy Đối Thôn (152 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Night: the harbour lamps and the Milky Way seem to merge, the pale ribs of the serpent glowing, and the city looks as if it rose out of the stars.
places.subject: The place: Tinh Hán Thành, the City of the Star River, a walled port on the inland sea. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at deep dusk; green-and-gold rolling hills with a thin river running down to a wide deep-blue sea at the right, grey rocky crags at the lower and upper corners, and a violet sky already showing the white band of the Milky Way. The city: a walled grid of about ten thousand grey-tile roofs inside grey walls about two and a half kilometres on a side, with a river gate and a harbour gate, warm lamps coming on in every street; wide avenues, a great harbour market, grain warehouses, pearl dealers' houses, a hall of the ruling sect, and the quarters of formation masters whose houses have chalk diagrams in their courtyards. Signature element: the breakwater, a long curving reef of great white arched ribs, the bones of an old sea-serpent, rising out of the water in a row of tall curved arches like the ribcage of a vast beast, with stone packed between them, about fifteen hundred paces long; a faint pale line of city formation glows along the walls and the bone reef, silver-blue threads of light; the harbour lamps and the Milky Way meeting at the horizon; a hundred vessels at the quays with lamps at their masts. Life at scale: tens of thousands of lit windows, tiny figures on the quays. Light: deep blue-violet dusk, warm lamplight, the pale bone arches glowing, a silver star-river overhead.

places.name: Song Kiều Trấn
places.size: A walled town of about 7,000 people on a river road: about 1,600 grey-tile roofs in a wall about 700 m across, two humpbacked stone bridges side by side, a toll house on a pier between them and a row of about 12 open ore scales.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), grassland at 0.5 km on a river. On the map: green-gold rolling hills with a river running diagonally from lower left to the right and to the sea, which shows at the right edge, grey rock ridges at the bottom, a small lake at the top left and conifers; the sea is a minor edge. Held by Thiên Xu Tông. Nearest: minor sect Chân Kim Các (127 km), hot spring Xuân Thủy Thang (146 km), village Thanh Mạch Thôn (160 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: A busy morning: carts roll in over one bridge and out over the other, and a clan elder sits in the toll house as he has every day of the year.
places.subject: The place: Song Kiều Trấn, the Twin Bridges Town, on a river road. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright morning; green-gold rolling hills with scattered dark conifer groves, a clear river running diagonally across the frame from lower left towards a sea strip at the right edge, grey rock ridges at the foot of the frame and a patch of rust-red hill at the left. The town: a walled square of grey stone about seven hundred paces on a side with gate towers at the road ends, about sixteen hundred grey-tile roofs in neat rows, and a market square behind the bridges where a row of about twelve open ore scales stands under a long tiled roof, with miners in dark clothing lined up with sacks and assayers in grey watching the needles in public view; a clan hall with a broad courtyard, an inn row, a smithy street. Signature element: two humpbacked stone bridges cross the river side by side, each about eighty paces long, one for carts going in and one for carts going out, with a small toll house on a pier between them; both bridges carry slow lines of ore carts, oxen and walkers in one direction each, a clean continuous flow; locals cross by one and come home by the other. Life at scale: a busy toll town, hundreds of tiny carters and miners. Light: clear gold morning light from the upper left, the river glinting under the arches, long soft shadows of the bridges.

places.name: Thủy Đối Thôn
places.size: A mill village of about 200 people: about 40 white-roofed houses along a fast stream, a row of about 12 waterwheels driving long trip-hammers under open sheds, flour dust whitening every roof.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), grassland at 0.2 km on a fast stream. On the map: green-gold hills with a stream running diagonally to a deep-blue sea at the right, grey crags at the bottom edge. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; the mills have ground Thanh Mạch's wheat for Tinh Hán Thành since 700. Nearest: spirit vein Thanh Lưu Mạch (79 km), spirit vein Triều Tịch Mạch (141 km), city Tinh Hán Thành (152 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: New Year's night: the wheels are stilled and in the silence the hammers hang over their mortars, and a baby wakes at the quiet.
places.subject: The place: Thủy Đối Thôn, the Water Mill Village, on a fast stream. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright morning; green-gold rolling hills with a fast clear stream running diagonally across the frame toward a deep-blue sea at the right, a few dark conifer clumps and grey crags at the lower edge. The village: about forty houses with white-powdered grey-tile roofs strung along the stream, with small yards and drying racks; a granary with a raised floor, a cooperage, a bakery with a plume, a hall of the miller's guild, a sack-sewing court and a wharf for flat barges loaded with flour. Signature element: along the stream stand a row of about twelve big timber waterwheels, each turning slowly in a race of white water, and each driving long wooden trip-hammers that rise and fall into stone mortars under open sheds with low roofs, a dozen hammers to a shed, thudding all day; flour dust whitens the roofs, the lanes and the nearby grass as if with frost, and the white dust drifts down the stream like smoke; carts of wheat sacks arriving in a line from the hills and carts of flour leaving for the city. Tiny millers in white-powdered aprons. Life at scale: a loud, white, rhythmic village. Light: soft bright morning light from the upper left, the water flashing white at the wheels, long pale shadows. Below the last wheel the stream widens and runs clear and fast between grassy banks toward the sea at the edge of the frame, where a line of barges waits to load, and children chase each other along the mill-race walls through drifting white flour dust.
